stem: Eklavya's tea mix has $4$ litres of concentrate and $6$ litres of water. He wants a concentrate-to-water ratio $4:9$ by adding only water.

parts.text: Which claim correctly finds how much water to add?

options.text: Concentrate stays $4$ litres. For ratio $4:9$, water must be $9$ litres, so add $9-6=3$ litres of water.
The changing component is water, so ignore the fixed concentrate and repartition the original $10$ litres.
Add $9$ litres of water because $9$ is the new ratio part printed for water.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Only water is added, so concentrate stays 4 L. Target water is 9 L; add 9−6=3 L.

teacher.key_rationale: Keep concentrate fixed at 4 L. Target water for 4:9 is 9 L, so add 3 L. Repartitioning the original total omits the fixed-component condition. Grabbing the printed 9 as the addend is a surface error.
